name: simbio
title: Showcase: viva-simbio — simbio CRN/ODE integration as a pluggable engine
description: viva-simbio bridges simbio (an Antimony/SBML reaction-network simulator built on poincare) into process-bigraph as a process that integrates a CRN against shared concentration and parameter stores. This showcase proves the engine on the classic Lotka-Volterra oscillator, with the Brusselator and repressilator available as additional registered composites.
question: Does viva-simbio expose the simbio chemical-reaction-network ODE engine as a process-bigraph process that integrates an Antimony model and emits real species trajectories?
hypothesis: Wrapping simbio as a process-bigraph process and integrating a Lotka-Volterra predator-prey Antimony model should produce sustained, bounded population oscillations — both species staying positive and the prey showing repeated peaks — using the real simbio ODE solver.

executive.what_is_this: A demonstration that the simbio reaction-network simulator can be driven as a plug-in engine inside process-bigraph. It integrates a predator-prey model and reports the two populations over time, showing the characteristic boom-and-bust oscillation.
executive.verdict: The Lotka-Volterra composite runs simbio end to end and produces sustained, bounded predator-prey oscillation (both species stay positive; prey peaks 3 times over t in [0,40]) — the acceptance band met in a clean-venv run of the pinned engine.
executive.verdict_detail: Study lotka-volterra: over t in [0, 40] (161 emitted rows), prey ranges 0.506-13.59 and predator 0.916-6.16, both strictly positive, with 3 prey peaks above 5.0 (observed on pbg-simbio @ main / simbio 1.1.0, 2026-11-27).

scientific_argument.main_claim: simbio can be exposed as a reusable process-bigraph process that integrates a real Antimony reaction network and emits correct, bounded dynamical trajectories.
evidence_for: The predator-prey populations stay positive and oscillate with multiple sustained cycles, the textbook Lotka-Volterra signature.
The Brusselator composite independently shows sustained oscillation (X amplitude ~3.4), confirming the engine drives more than one CRN.
evidence_against: These are canonical demonstration models, not calibrated biological systems; they exercise the engine, not a specific biological claim.
caveats: simbio/poincare 1.3 dropped the solve() kwargs this bridge depends on, so the showcase pins simbio==1.1.* / poincare==1.1.* to keep the engine runnable.
